baseline_rule: A row counts only when it carries a verdict and action; at least one source that is a `mined` SOURCES row whose used-by names the entry and that was either opened 2026-10-22 or had its `recheck` updated in place this round with the change logged old -> new in corpus/lessons/round-25.md; a located quote of at most 25 words recorded in that lesson's Gate; at least one pointer into the frozen capture whose line text is unique in the capture and is not a section header, command echo or exit line; and a SKILL.md decision-table row, appended this round, that names the row id.

finding_id_vocabulary.note: expected_finding_id names the finding the PRODUCTION checker must emit. The self-check oracle in fixtures/oracle-check-memory-pressure.py uses a different, coarser vocabulary (a single MP-ROW-PROBLEM id plus a problem tag on the site); oracle_problem names the oracle tag this seat's own self-check asserts. The two vocabularies are deliberately separate: the production ids are a contract with the C2 build seat, the oracle tags are a self-check of the fixtures alone.
finding_id_vocabulary.production_ids_are: a proposal sent to the C2 build seat on 2026-10-22 and to be reconciled with the tool's actual ids before the wave-2 sweep

mutations.breaks_rule: a cited source must be a `mined` SOURCES row
the cited source's used-by cell must name the entry
a cited source must be opened 2026-10-22, or have its recheck updated in place this round with the change logged old -> new in the lesson
the located quote recorded in the lesson Gate is at most 25 words
mutations.note: The operation writes 26 words into the quote cell, but the Gate reader takes the whole cell, whose word count is 37; the expectation therefore names the observed word count. The tool reads the same 37 words, so the two agree.

mutations.breaks_rule: a capture pointer must not resolve to a `### ` section header
a capture pointer must not resolve to a `$ ` command echo
a capture pointer must not resolve to an `[exit ` line
a capture pointer's line text must be unique in the capture
the capture file must hash to the pinned sha256
SKILL.md must carry a decision-table row naming the row id
a quote the row carries must be the Gate quote of a source the row lists, and must be at most 25 words

params.replacement: a quote the Gate does not record for this source

mutations.breaks_rule: a corpus/SOURCES.md row whose cell count differs from the registry header's is malformed and its columns cannot be named

notes: Every mutation breaks exactly one counting rule. M01 to M08 and M10 each disqualify exactly one MP row, so verified_rows falls from 6 to 5. M09 is the exception: a capture digest mismatch is a document-level fault that the oracle reports as a finding on the capture itself rather than as a row problem, so expected_verified_rows is null and expected_rows_broken is empty for it.

The baseline cites exactly one SOURCES row and one Gate quote per MP row, and the six rows use six distinct source ids, so a single-cell change to one registry row or one Gate quote can only disqualify the one row that cites it.

A pointer mutation replaces the whole capture_pointers list of its row. The rule under test is 'at least one qualifying pointer', so a mutant that left a good pointer behind would not exercise that rule at all.
Baseline capture pointers are unique, non-structural lines of the frozen capture, so that M05 to M08 each break exactly one pointer rule.

The M05 target line 12 is a `### ` section header, M06 target line 28 is a `$ ` command echo, M07 target line 74 is the only unique `[exit ` line in the capture, and M08 target line 21 is a value line whose text occurs twice (lines 21 and 29).

expected_finding_id is the contract with the C2 build seat; it was proposed to that seat on 2026-10-22 and must be reconciled with the tool's actual ids before the wave-2 sweep. The aliases table lets the runner accept a small family of equivalent names.

M09 is the exception to the 6 -> 5 expectation: a capture digest mismatch is a document-level fault that the tool reports as a finding on the capture itself rather than as a row problem, so expected_verified_rows is null and expected_rows_broken is empty for it.

M11 replaces the entry's own quote for MP4 with a text the lesson Gate does not record for that source, so the row asserts a quote no cited page supplies. The production checker reports MP-QUOTE-MISMATCH for it, and that finding is blocking, so MP4 stops verifying and verified_rows falls from 6 to 5. This mutant is what pins the stricter R3: under the earlier advisory semantics the same mutant left the count at 6. Note that truncating the Gate quote instead is NOT an equivalent mutant: the comparison accepts a quote that is contained in the Gate quote or the other way round, so a shorter Gate quote still matches the longer entry quote.

M12 drops one cell from the S115 registry row, so its cell count differs from the 11-column header's and its columns cannot be named. The checker reports MP-SOURCE-ROW-SHAPE for it and, by design, does not also report the status/opened/used-by findings that a shifted read would have produced. This is the one mutant that must assert an exact finding set rather than the presence of an id.
